tasks.short: Investigate website problems, fix suitable issues, and route others to the right specialist.

steps.what: Read test failures and customer feedback, then record a problem report.

loop.input: Customer feedback and test evidence, with attachments treated as untrusted data.
loop.output: Draft problem report with symptoms, affected page, reproduction clues and source references.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; designer confirms meaning and sensitive-data removal.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per report; incomplete cases return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured test failures import directly, but customer descriptions need interpretation.

steps.what: Reproduce the reported behaviour in a browser and capture evidence.
Assess impact, choose priority, and decide who should correct the problem.
Correct content or component settings, or assign a specialist correction ticket.
Review regression evidence and approve or reject the staged correction.
Publish approved corrections and update the problem report or specialist handoff.

tasks.design: Connect {HELPDESK}, {PROJECT} and {CMS}; import structured failures directly and use a bounded reader for free-text feedback. Deterministic browser checks prepare reproduction evidence, approved correction recipes stage simple fixes, and routing rules create specialist tickets; publication consumes the web lead's recorded approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback lacked consistent reproduction details, and issue records were separated from site changes and test evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces, browser automation and reusable correction recipes make the connections practical. A bounded reader can turn varied feedback into a reviewable report.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent failures, ambiguous customer intent and commercial impact still require investigation. Corrections outside approved recipes need a specialist.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparently small defect damages trust or blocks an important customer journey.
tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time copying reports and repeating known checks. The team can delegate prioritisation within an agreed repair budget; broader release authority needs explicit delegation.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Group customer friction by journey stage.
reach.learn: Qualitative coding, sampling bias and distinguishing frequent complaints from severe barriers.

evidence.claim: Ticket tools can suggest categories and priorities, supporting assisted feedback intake.
Known browser journeys and narrowly defined correction recipes can run deterministically.

assumptions: Typical work uses issue records and browser inspection more than meetings; the supplied means shares overstate meeting time.
Remaining time is a planning estimate; reproduction failures and unfamiliar fixes return to a person.
Specialist code corrections are performed under the supporting-code task; full regression testing belongs to the website-testing task.
Build ranges cover one reusable starter for one site. Consultation effort is included where applicable; external waiting time is additional.
GDPR and EU AI Act obligations apply. Employee consultation depends on national rules and whether staff activity is observed.
unknowns: Which interfaces and staging permissions are available.
Which corrections can be expressed as approved recipes.
Whether customer feedback contains personal data.
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply.
research_questions: How reliably can fixed replay recipes reproduce the main classes of reported website problems?
new_work: Review extracted reports and remove unnecessary personal data.
Handle unsuccessful reproductions and incorrect routing.
Maintain correction recipes, permissions and interface mappings.

tasks.short: Design, assemble and maintain website pages, media and navigation.

steps.what: Review the brief, audience needs, content and website constraints.
Create layouts and navigation in a visual design editor.
Prepare approved copy, image crops, alternative text and page metadata.

loop.input: Approved copy, media assets, page context and editorial constraints.
loop.output: Draft alternative text and metadata alongside deterministic image derivatives.
loop.check: Validate lengths and asset references; designer checks meaning, image purpose and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per asset; unresolved meaning returns to the content owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Image resizing is deterministic, but useful alternative text depends on the image's purpose in context.

steps.what: Assemble pages, navigation and reusable components in the website editor.
Review staged pages and test evidence, then decide whether to publish.
Publish approved pages and record the website revision.

tasks.design: Configure reusable page types, navigation rules and approval states in {CMS}, with approved assets supplied from {DOCS}. A deterministic asset pipeline handles crops and file checks, a bounded loop drafts contextual descriptions, and approved pages publish with revision records in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent components and scattered assets made each page a small custom project. Custom design decisions could not be reduced to templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable page schemas and asset rules remove repeated assembly work. AI-assisted coding can help build missing utilities, while editorial drafting stays bounded.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive design, information architecture and accessible interaction require judgement. A weak component library makes initial setup expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a visual and interaction direction that fits the audience, message and brand.

ambition.what: An accessible campaign-page service for small internal campaign teams.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends more of the week shaping journeys and reviewing assembled pages. They can gain authority to accept routine page requests within agreed templates and capacity.

reach.task: Shape a page's message hierarchy before layout begins.
reach.learn: Content structure, plain language and editorial acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Translate search intent into landing-page requirements.
reach.learn: Intent mapping, crawlability and separating search assumptions from measured outcomes.

evidence.claim: Reusable content types, components and publication workflows can reduce repeated page assembly.
Coding assistants can help implement supporting utilities, with human oversight.

assumptions: The company maintains a public marketing website with staging and reusable components.
Editor and browser work dominate routine delivery; the supplied meeting share is too high for this task.
Custom component programming and full regression testing are counted in their separate tasks.
Build estimates cover a reusable starter, not a full website redesign, and overlap with supporting-code work.
GDPR applies to embedded forms and tracking; EU AI Act duties depend on deployed functionality. National rules determine any employee consultation.
unknowns: How complete the component library and content schemas are.
Who can approve content, branding and publication.
Which languages, accessibility requirements and audience groups the site must support.
Whether publication changes introduce tracking or employee observation.
research_questions: Which page patterns can preserve design quality through configuration alone?
How much editorial review do contextual alternative-text drafts require?
new_work: Maintain page schemas, asset rules and component examples.
Review generated descriptions and unusual image crops.
Handle requests that fall outside supported page patterns.
Monitor published pages for broken assets and content drift.

tasks.short: Write and review supporting website code, then merge tested changes.

steps.what: Read the change request and agree behaviour and acceptance criteria.
Inspect existing source, dependencies and component usage in a code editor.
Create standard component files, imports and configuration in a code editor.
Implement component behaviour, styling and focused tests in a code editor.

loop.input: Approved specification, selected source files, component conventions and permitted file paths.
loop.output: Isolated code patch and focused tests.
loop.check: Compile, lint, scan dependencies and run tests; designer checks behaviour and test independence.
loop.stop: At most two repair attempts within ten minutes; return the patch and failures to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle scaffolding, but application-specific behaviour requires interpreting requirements and existing code.

steps.what: Run build, code-quality and focused test commands in a development environment.
Review the code diff, behaviour and check results in the source repository.
Merge approved code and update the change request.

tasks.design: Use deterministic templates and a bounded coding loop in the development toolchain represented by {OTHER}; keep each patch isolated with no production credentials. Configured checks validate the patch, a developer approves merging, and the integration updates {PROJECT} before website regression testing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supporting code varied by application, while reusable scaffolding and checks were often incomplete. Automating bespoke changes required too much custom logic.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance can produce bounded patches against existing conventions. Deterministic generators and existing checks handle the repeatable parts.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear requirements, legacy dependencies and tests that confirm the wrong behaviour. Generated code still needs security and maintainability review.
tasks.human_edge: Defining correct behaviour and recognising changes that create hidden complexity or weaken accessibility.

ambition.what: A small-change component service for campaign teams.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time on scaffolding and more on interaction behaviour and code review. They can gain responsibility for accepting bounded component requests, while merge and release permissions remain separately assigned.

reach.task: Implement technical search requirements in reusable website components.
reach.learn: Rendering, structured metadata and performance measurement.

evidence.claim: Coding assistants provide completion and review capabilities, with oversight expected.
Field experiments found productivity improvements, but they do not establish this task's expected time saving.
A controlled study found experienced developers slower with the tools studied, so coding gains need local measurement.

assumptions: The designer writes client-side supporting code and has a development environment and source repository, represented by {OTHER}.
Code-editor work dominates; the supplied meeting and document shares are poor priors for daily implementation.
Estimates cover bounded component changes, not arbitrary application development.
Build ranges cover reusable tooling and overlap with website assembly and testing; they should not simply be added.
GDPR governs any personal data supplied as context. EU AI Act obligations apply as relevant; employee observation or evaluation requires separate assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Which languages, build tools and repository permissions are used.
Whether existing tests detect meaningful behavioural regressions.
Which source files and data may be supplied to a model.
Whether merge automatically triggers production publication.
research_questions: Which change types show a measured reduction in total implementation and review time?
Which checks catch defects that generated tests consistently miss?
new_work: Maintain templates, context selection and permitted file paths.
Review generated patches and the validity of generated tests.
Track rework and escaped defects alongside coding time.
Update toolchain dependencies and access controls.

tasks.short: Run scheduled and revision-triggered website checks, investigate failures, and report release risks.

steps.what: Check the test schedule and identify revisions ready for testing.
Select affected journeys, browser coverage and accessibility checks from the test plan.
Execute repeatable checks in browsers and website-testing tools.
Explore changed journeys and inspect keyboard use, readability and visual behaviour.
Separate genuine failures from unstable tests and combine the findings.
Create defect records with screenshots, affected revisions and reproduction details.
Review unresolved failures and record the release-risk recommendation.

tasks.design: Trigger deterministic browser, link and accessibility checks from {PROJECT} revisions and schedules, using isolated test infrastructure represented by {OTHER}. Attach evidence and deduplicated failures to {PROJECT}; people select novel coverage, explore usability and recommend release action, with publication approval handled at the publishing step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual scripts, changing page selectors and unreliable test data made automation costly to maintain. Visual quality and usability could not be settled by pass/fail checks alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable browser fixtures, stable component identifiers and standard checkers make repeatable execution practical. AI-assisted coding can reduce the setup effort without putting a model in every test run.
tasks.still_hard: Unstable environments, external services, representative device coverage and meaningful accessibility testing. Automated checks cannot establish overall usability or accessibility conformance.
tasks.human_edge: Finding surprising interaction failures and deciding whether a technically passing journey is understandable and usable.

ambition.what: A release-risk assessment for every candidate website revision.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeating scripted checks toward exploratory testing and coverage decisions. The analyst can recommend release readiness more often; final publication rights do not change automatically.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Test whether target users understand a changed website journey.
reach.learn: Moderated usability methods, participant selection and interpreting small samples.

evidence.claim: Scheduled browser, link and rule-based accessibility checks can execute deterministically.
Test tooling can use models to draft plans, tests and repairs; this is an optional authoring aid.

assumptions: A staging environment and synthetic test identities are available.
Repeatable execution is a substantial share despite the supplied human classification; exploratory judgement stays human.
Testing tools and browsers are represented by {OTHER}; documentation guides testing but does not dominate execution time.
Automated tests cannot submit real orders, contact customers or change production records.
Build estimates cover an initial set of critical journeys and overlap with supporting-code setup.
GDPR governs captured screenshots and logs. EU AI Act duties apply where relevant; national rules determine consultation if staff behaviour is recorded.
unknowns: Which journeys, browsers and devices require coverage.
Whether test data and environments are reliable.
Which accessibility checks already exist and who performs manual assessment.
Whether recordings or screenshots expose customer or employee data.
research_questions: Which critical journeys can run reliably without production side effects?
Which failure categories produce the most false alarms?
Which important accessibility barriers remain outside automated coverage?
new_work: Maintain selectors, fixtures and browser coverage.
Investigate unstable tests without weakening assertions to obtain a pass.
Review evidence retention and redact captured personal data.
Refresh exploratory coverage after significant journey changes.

role.altitude: The role moves toward interaction design, reusable components, exploratory evaluation and evidence-based release recommendations. Routine assembly, reporting and repeatable checks shrink; additional prioritisation or acceptance rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Editors: shape message hierarchy and page acceptance criteria.
Search Marketing Strategists: connect search intent with technically sound landing pages.
Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists: turn observed journey friction into focused research.
skills_to_grow: Accessible interaction design and manual evaluation
Deterministic browser testing and test-data management
Privacy-aware handling of feedback and test evidence
role.ambitious_version: Run a reusable website improvement service: campaign teams receive accessible page patterns, bounded component changes and regular journey-risk assessments, while the designer concentrates on audience needs and difficult design decisions.
